scope: All 186 current model features have a source-review entry. Documented identities and floor relationships are distinguished from inferred bank correspondence and unmeasured geometry. This is not an exhaustive inventory of every physical station asset.
sourcePolicy: Use operator diagrams for equipment and floors, dated work notices for closures, facility guides for destination links, and PLATEAU/GSI for geographic context. Preserve publication, observation and proposed-completion dates separately.

sources.title: Tokyu floor plans and isometric map
sources.scope: B1–B5 plans, exit codes, lift identifiers, escalator arrows, gates and amenities.
sources.caveat: Exit-direction inset is dated 2024-08-30. Diagram coordinates are not survey coordinates.

sources.title: Metro isometric station map
sources.scope: Ginza 3F/2F and the underground station stack.
sources.caveat: Older than Tokyu’s plan; the user’s English illustration is dated 2025-11. Retrieved through the official page after direct-download 403.

sources.title: Station accessibility facilities
sources.scope: Lift routes, escalator directions and accessible toilet facilities.
sources.caveat: Underground text still uses legacy exit numbers such as 13a and 15. Do not equate them with current A/B/C codes without a dated crosswalk.
sources.inspectionMethod: Official page text or browser inspection

sources.caveat: Printed warning: station works can alter the plan. Retrieved through the official page after direct-download 403.

sources.title: JR Shibuya station facilities

sources.caveat: Senior-car route restrictions are specific to that equipment, not a general ban on all wheelchair routes.

sources.title: Keio station floor plan

sources.title: Keio isometric map with closure overlay

sources.caveat: The newer floor-plan publication date does not establish completion of the lift works.

sources.title: West-exit lift construction notice

sources.caveat: As checked on 2026-09-19, the planned finish is still in the future. No completion or opening confirmation established.

sources.title: Shibuya City guide map
sources.scope: 1:10,000 city map: roads, railways, destinations and surrounding district.
sources.caveat: Map title says 2025; footer says issued February 2026. Downloaded PDF is a raster page without a /VP geospatial transform; no entrance coordinates were extracted.

sources.title: Walkable City Shibuya infrastructure booklet
sources.scope: Printed pp.12–15 show district connections, proposed decks and free passages; pp.16–17 describe vertical circulation.
sources.caveat: Completion illustrations include future works, some labelled FY2027 onward. Do not convert the illustrated future network into current open routes.

sources.title: Barrier-free implementation plan, revised edition
sources.scope: Printed pp.5–6 (PDF pp.11–12): JR, Keio, Tokyu and Ginza station improvement entries.
sources.caveat: Station section explicitly reports status as of end-January 2024. A March 2026 cover is not a 2026 equipment-status survey.

sources.title: Shibuya barrier-free map guide
sources.scope: Public map guide and sampled live-map lift record near Hikarie, including its displayed provenance and update date.
sources.caveat: Official facility markers and user contributions differ. Sampled Hikarie priority-lift record is a WheeLog contribution last updated 2019-02-08; not accepted as a current surveyed control. Individual map records were not exhaustively checked.
sources.inspectionMethod: Official page text or browser inspection

sources.title: Public pedestrian spatial network catalog
sources.scope: Downloaded Shibuya south GeoJSON: 1,641 nodes and 1,823 links with floor and accessibility attribute codes.
sources.caveat: Historic network; no current exit or lift IDs in node attributes. Zero independently matched control points accepted. Raw coded attributes were not interpreted as metres or equipment counts.

sources.caveat: Three building-centre fit controls give 25.7 m RMS mismatch, not independent entrance accuracy. Five other destination feature identities remain unresolved.

findings.title: Hikarie gates and slope
findings.detail: Moved the Hikarie gate concourse, B5 interface and adjoining circulation to B3, separated the B2 Miyamasuzaka area, and added the B2–B3 slope. Reconnected the B4 banks and public transitions. Shapes and slope gradients remain illustrative.

findings.title: Exit landing floors
findings.detail: A12 now has a B2 branch; exit B1 has a B3 approach plus lifts 20a/20b; B5 meets Hikarie at B3; B7 has its own B1 landing. C1/C2/C3 branches are distinct. C3 floor correspondence remains provisional.

findings.title: B5 platform numbering
findings.detail: Corrected the shared dataset: western island 5–6, eastern island 3–4. Both the 2D diagram and 3D views inherit these labels; geometry remains schematic.

findings.title: JR gate floors and lifts
findings.detail: Central and New South gate areas are on 3F; Hachiko and South are on 1F. Added six source-lettered lifts A–F with explicit stops, platform connections and gate markers. These are schematic relationships, not an as-built circulation graph.

findings.title: Keio levels and published closures
findings.detail: Added West 1F, Central 2F, Avenue 4F, the arrival-only platform, external Central lift and stairs A–F. C/D are visibly closed in the source; Avenue hours are recorded. West lift works remain a planned marker, not an open lift.

findings.title: All 20 drawn exit codes matched
findings.detail: A0–A8, A12, B1–B7 and C1–C3 match the reviewed Tokyu plan. This corrects the earlier claim that the plan contained additional exit groups. Twenty badges do not enumerate every physical doorway, approach level or JR/Keio gate.

findings.title: Equipment identities, stops and access rules
findings.detail: Source-identified lifts and lettered stairs are represented, with explicit stops or range endpoints, published hours and closure state. Lift 21 does not appear on B1. Ginza paid and unpaid lifts are separate. Generic banks still lack an individual asset match; directions and live availability remain incomplete.

findings.title: Gates and station facilities
findings.detail: Added 15 named gates and 19 amenity markers covering toilets, baby care, AEDs, lockers, tickets and information, plus one construction marker. These are selected identifiable features; a complete amenity, tactile-guidance and continuous paid-boundary survey is still needed.

findings.title: Current-looking pages can contain old data
findings.detail: Metro’s underground accessibility text uses legacy exit numbers. The city’s March 2026 barrier-free plan reports station status from January 2024. The November 2024 infrastructure booklet includes future completion diagrams.

findings.title: Geographic registration remains unverified
findings.detail: City maps and historic pedestrian GeoJSON add geographic context, but no independently matched entrance or corner was established. The existing PLATEAU fit remains 25.7 m RMS across three building centres; floor heights are illustrative.
